inspiration.observed_pattern: A qualification CTE counts distinct categories across several LEFT JOINs, keeps groups with HAVING, and a second date-filtered CTE restricts the final rows through an IN subquery.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original member-activity report. A member qualifies after checking out items from at least two distinct categories; a separate recent-orders CTE limits the report to members active in a fixed date range. Duplicate checkout rows, members without enough categories, and qualifying members without recent orders exercise distinct counting, LEFT JOIN preservation, HAVING, and CTE-backed semi-join filtering.

fixture_notes: Member 10 has duplicate checkout rows spanning three categories and a recent order; member 20 has two categories but only an old order; member 30 has one category and a recent order; member 40 has no checkouts and a recent order. Only member 10 should survive both CTE filters.
determinism_notes: Member IDs and order dates are fixed, and the final report is ordered by member ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE members (member_id INT PRIMARY KEY, member_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE categories (category_id INT PRIMARY KEY, category_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE items (item_id INT PRIMARY KEY, category_id INT NOT NULL, item_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE checkouts (checkout_id INT PRIMARY KEY, member_id INT NOT NULL, item_id INT NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, member_id INT NOT NULL, ordered_on DATE NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH qualifying_members AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.member_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.category_id) AS category_count FROM members m LEFT JOIN checkouts ch ON ch.member_id = m.member_id LEFT JOIN items i ON i.item_id = ch.item_id LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = i.category_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.member_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.category_id) >= 2), recent_orders AS (SELECT member_id FROM orders WHERE ordered_on BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-31') SELECT q.member_id, q.member_name, q.category_count FROM qualifying_members q WHERE q.member_id IN (SELECT r.member_id FROM recent_orders r) ORDER BY q.member_id

checks.sql: SELECT member_id, member_name FROM members ORDER BY member_id
SELECT checkout_id, member_id, item_id FROM checkouts ORDER BY checkout_id
SELECT order_id, member_id, ordered_on FROM orders ORDER BY order_id
